title: Lakehouse and Governance Platform: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Lakehouse and Governance Platform: Visual Guide

1. Unbundling The Lake | a bundled-warehouse vs lakehouse toggle over five concerns - storage, query access, metadata, governance, distribution - each row naming the earlier lesson it builds on and the service that owns it now | storage, query access, metadata, governance and distribution are separate problems with separate services, and most wrong answers in this domain are the right service for a different one of the five

2. Delegating File Access | a slider over 1-40 analysts with a direct-bucket-grants vs BigLake-connection switch, plus a toggle that leaves one analyst holding a broad Cloud Storage role | BigLake gives object permission to one connection service account and table permission to everyone else, which is what makes row-level, column-level and masking policy real - and a single leftover direct bucket role silently defeats all of it

3. The Metadata Cache | object count from 1,000 to 5,000,000 against cache OFF / automatic / manual, with a maximum-staleness dial and the four-step manual refresh sequence | metadata caching buys discovery time and spends freshness, so maximum staleness is a contract you choose and manual refresh belongs inside the pipeline before readiness is published

4. Zones And Aspects | a raw vs curated zone selector over a lake-zone-asset tree, with technical, operational and business metadata switched on and off to produce a trust verdict | a Dataplex lake is logical structure over assets that move nowhere, raw and curated zones state different contracts, and a catalog entry needs technical, operational and business metadata together before anyone can trust the table

5. Copies Or Links | 1-40 consumers under scheduled exports vs an Analytics Hub listing, with a dataset-listing vs Pub/Sub-topic-listing switch showing stored copies, pipelines, what lands in the consumer project and who pays | subscribing creates a read-only linked dataset instead of a copy per consumer, a topic listing creates a linked Pub/Sub subscription that delivers messages instead, and exports still win when a consumer needs independent retention, offline access or isolation from publisher changes
